classes.label: entity
classes.definition: (Elucidation) An entity is anything that exists or has existed or will exist
examples: Julius Caesar; the Second World War; your body mass index; Verdi's Requiem

classes.label: continuant
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A continuant is an entity that persists, endures, or continues to exist through time while maintaining its identity
examples: A human being; a tennis ball; a cave; a region of space; someone's temperature

classes.label: occurrent
classes.definition: (Elucidation) An occurrent is an entity that unfolds itself in time or it is the start or end of such an entity or it is a temporal or spatiotemporal region
examples: As for process, history, process boundary, spatiotemporal region, zero-dimensional temporal region, one-dimensional temporal region, temporal interval, temporal instant.

classes.label: independent continuant
classes.definition: b is an independent continuant =Def b is a continuant & there is no c such that b specifically depends on c or b generically depends on c
examples: An atom; a molecule; an organism; a heart; a chair; the bottom right portion of a human torso; a leg; the interior of your mouth; a spatial region; an orchestra

classes.label: spatial region
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A spatial region is a continuant entity that is a continuant part of the spatial projection of a portion of spacetime at a given time
examples: As for zero-dimensional spatial region, one-dimensional spatial region, two-dimensional spatial region, three-dimensional spatial region

classes.label: temporal region
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A temporal region is an occurrent over which processes can unfold
examples: As for zero-dimensional temporal region and one-dimensional temporal region

classes.label: two-dimensional spatial region
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A two-dimensional spatial region is a spatial region that is a whole consisting of a surface together with zero or more surfaces which may have spatial regions of lower dimension as parts
examples: The surface of a sphere-shaped part of space; an infinitely thin plane in space

classes.label: spatiotemporal region
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A spatiotemporal region is an occurrent that is an occurrent part of spacetime 'Spacetime' here refers to the maximal instance of the universal spatiotemporal region.
examples: The spatiotemporal region occupied by the development of a cancer tumour; the spatiotemporal region occupied by an orbiting satellite

classes.label: process
classes.definition: (Elucidation) p is a process means p is an occurrent that has some temporal proper part and for some time t, p has some material entity as participant
examples: An act of selling; the life of an organism; a process of sleeping; a process of cell-division; a beating of the heart; a process of meiosis; the taxiing of an aircraft; the programming of a computer

classes.label: disposition
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A disposition b is a realizable entity such that if b ceases to exist then its bearer is physically changed & b's realization occurs when and because this bearer is in some special physical circumstances & this realization occurs in virtue of the bearer's physical make-up
examples: An atom of element X has the disposition to decay to an atom of element Y; the cell wall is disposed to transport cellular material through endocytosis and exocytosis; certain people have a predisposition to colon cancer; children are innately disposed to categorize objects in certain ways

classes.label: realizable entity
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A realizable entity is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in some independent continuant which is not a spatial region & which is of a type some instances of which are realized in processes of a correlated type
examples: The role of being a doctor; the role of this boundary to delineate where Utah and Colorado meet; the function of your reproductive organs; the disposition of your blood to coagulate; the disposition of this piece of metal to conduct electricity

classes.label: zero-dimensional spatial region
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A zero-dimensional spatial region is one or a collection of more than one spatially disjoint points in space
examples: The spatial region occupied at some time instant by the North Pole

classes.label: quality
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A quality is a specifically dependent continuant that, in contrast to roles and dispositions, does not require any further process in order to be realized
examples: The colour of a tomato; the ambient temperature of this portion of air; the length of the circumference of your waist; the shape of your nose; the shape of your nostril; the mass of this piece of gold

classes.label: specifically dependent continuant
classes.definition: b is a specifically dependent continuant =Def b is a continuant & there is some independent continuant c which is not a spatial region & which is such that b specifically depends on c
examples: (with multiple bearers) John's love for Mary; the ownership relation between John and this statue; the relation of authority between John and his subordinates

(with one bearer) The mass of this tomato; the pink colour of a medium rare piece of grilled filet mignon at its centre; the smell of this portion of mozzarella; the disposition of this fish to decay; the role of being a doctor; the function of this heart to pump blood; the shape of this hole

classes.label: role
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A role b is a realizable entity such that b exists because there is some single bearer that is in some special physical, social, or institutional set of circumstances in which this bearer does not have to be & b is not such that, if it ceases to exist, then the physical make-up of the bearer is thereby changed
examples: The priest role; the student role; the role of subject in a clinical trial; the role of a stone in marking a property boundary; the role of a boundary to demarcate two neighbouring administrative territories; the role of a building in serving as a military target

classes.label: fiat object part
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A fiat object part b is a material entity & such that if b exists then it is continuant part of some object c & demarcated from the remainder of c by one or more fiat surfaces
examples: The upper and lower lobes of the left lung; the dorsal and ventral surfaces of the body; the Western hemisphere of the Earth; the FMA:regional parts of an intact human body

classes.label: one-dimensional spatial region
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A one-dimensional spatial region is a whole consisting of a line together with zero or more lines which may have points as parts
examples: An edge of a cube-shaped portion of space; a line connecting two points; two parallel lines extended in space

classes.label: object aggregate
classes.definition: (Elucidation) An object aggregate is a material entity consisting exactly of a plurality (≥1) of objects as member parts which together form a unit 'Exactly' means that there are no parts of the object aggregate other than its member parts.
examples: The aggregate of the musicians in a symphony orchestra and their instruments; the aggregate of bearings in a constant velocity axle joint; the nitrogen atoms in the atmosphere; a collection of cells in a blood biobank

classes.label: three-dimensional spatial region
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A three-dimensional spatial region is a whole consisting of a spatial volume together with zero or more spatial volumes which may have spatial regions of lower dimension as parts
examples: A cube-shaped region of space; a sphere-shaped region of space; the region of space occupied by all and only the planets in the solar system at some point in time

classes.label: site
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A site is a three-dimensional immaterial entity whose boundaries either (partially or wholly) coincide with the boundaries of one or more material entities or have locations determined in relation to some material entity
examples: A hole in a portion of cheese; a rabbit hole; the Grand Canyon; the Piazza San Marco; the kangaroo-joey-containing hole of a kangaroo pouch; your left nostril (a fiat part - the opening - of your left nasal cavity); the lumen of your gut; the hold of a ship; the interior of the trunk of your car; hole in an engineered floor joist

classes.label: object
classes.definition: (Elucidation) An object is a material entity which manifests causal unity & is of a type instances of which are maximal relative to the sort of causal unity manifested A description of three primary sorts of causal unity is provided in Basic Formal Ontology 2.0. Specification and User Guide
examples: An organism; a fish tank; a planet; a laptop; a valve; a block of marble; an ice cube

classes.label: generically dependent continuant
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A generically dependent continuant is an entity that exists in virtue of the fact that there is at least one of what may be multiple copies which is the content or the pattern that multiple copies would share
examples: The pdf file on your laptop; the pdf file that is a copy thereof on my laptop; the sequence of this protein molecule; the sequence that is a copy thereof in that protein molecule; the content that is shared by a string of dots and dashes written on a page and the transmitted Morse code signal; the content of a sentence; an engineering blueprint

classes.label: function
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A function is a disposition that exists in virtue of its bearer's physical make-up & this physical make-up is something the bearer possesses because it came into being either through evolution (in the case of natural biological entities) or through intentional design (in the case of artefacts) in order to realize processes of a certain sort
examples: The function of a hammer to drive in nails; the function of a heart pacemaker to regulate the beating of a heart through electricity

classes.label: process boundary
classes.definition: p is a process boundary =Def p is a temporal part of a process & p has no proper temporal parts
examples: The boundary between the 2nd and 3rd year of your life

classes.label: one-dimensional temporal region
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A one-dimensional temporal region is a temporal region that is a whole that has a temporal interval and zero or more temporal intervals and temporal instants as parts
examples: The temporal region during which a process occurs

classes.label: material entity
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A material entity is an independent continuant has some portion of matter as continuant part
examples: A human being; the undetached arm of a human being; an aggregate of human beings

classes.label: continuant fiat boundary
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A continuant fiat boundary b is an immaterial entity that is of zero, one or two dimensions & such that there is no time t when b has a spatial region as continuant part & whose location is determined in relation to some material entity
examples: As for fiat point, fiat line, fiat surface

classes.label: immaterial entity
classes.definition: b is an immaterial entity =Def b is an independent continuant which is such that there is no time t when it has a material entity as continuant part
examples: As for fiat point, fiat line, fiat surface, site

classes.label: fiat line
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A fiat line is a one-dimensional continuant fiat boundary that is continuous
examples: The Equator; all geopolitical boundaries; all lines of latitude and longitude; the median sulcus of your tongue; the line separating the outer surface of the mucosa of the lower lip from the outer surface of the skin of the chin

classes.label: Process Profile
classes.definition: An occurrent that is an occurrent part of some process by virtue of the rate, or pattern, or magnitude of change in an attribute of one or more participants of said process. b process_profile_of c holds when b proper_occurrent_part_of c& there is some proper_occurrent_part d of c which has no parts in common with b & is mutually dependent on b& is such that b, c and d occupy the same temporal region (axiom label in BFO2 Reference: [094-005])
examples: On a somewhat higher level of complexity are what we shall call rate process profiles, which are the targets of selective abstraction focused not on determinate quality magnitudes plotted over time, but rather on certain ratios between these magnitudes and elapsed times. A speed process profile, for example, is represented by a graph plotting against time the ratio of distance covered per unit of time. Since rates may change, and since such changes, too, may have rates of change, we have to deal here with a hierarchy of process profile universals at successive levels; One important sub-family of rate process profiles is illustrated by the beat or frequency profiles of cyclical processes, illustrated by the 60 beats per minute beating process of John’s heart, or the 120 beats per minute drumming process involved in one of John’s performances in a rock band, and so on. Each such process includes what we shall call a beat process profile instance as part, a subtype of rate process profile in which the salient ratio is not distance covered but rather number of beat cycles per unit of time. Each beat process profile instance instantiates the determinable universal beat process profile. But it also instantiates multiple more specialized universals at lower levels of generality, selected from rate process profilebeat process profileregular beat process profile3 bpm beat process profile4 bpm beat process profileirregular beat process profileincreasing beat process profileand so on.In the case of a regular beat process profile, a rate can be assigned in the simplest possible fashion by dividing the number of cycles by the length of the temporal region occupied by the beating process profile as a whole. Irregular process profiles of this sort, for example as identified in the clinic, or in the readings on an aircraft instrument panel, are often of diagnostic significance.; The simplest type of process profiles are what we shall call ‘quality process profiles’, which are the process profiles which serve as the foci of the sort of selective abstraction that is involved when measurements are made of changes in single qualities, as illustrated, for example, by process profiles of mass, temperature, aortic pressure, and so on.

classes.label: relational quality
classes.definition: b is a relational quality =Def b is a quality & there exists c and d such that c and d are not identical & b specifically depends on c & b specifically depends on d
examples: A marriage bond; an instance of love; an obligation between one person and another

classes.label: fiat surface
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A fiat surface is a two-dimensional continuant fiat boundary that is self-connected
examples: The surface of the Earth; the plane separating the smoking from the non-smoking zone in a restaurant

classes.label: fiat point
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A fiat point is a zero-dimensional continuant fiat boundary that consists of a single point
examples: The geographic North Pole; the quadripoint where the boundaries of Colorado, Utah, New Mexico and Arizona meet; the point of origin of some spatial coordinate system

classes.label: zero-dimensional temporal region
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A zero-dimensional temporal region is a temporal region that is a whole consisting of one or more separated temporal instants as parts
examples: A temporal region that is occupied by a process boundary; the moment at which a finger is detached in an industrial accident

classes.label: history
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A history is a process that is the sum of the totality of processes taking place in the spatiotemporal region occupied by the material part of a material entity
examples: The life of an organism from the beginning to the end of its existence

classes.label: temporal interval
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A temporal interval is a one-dimensional temporal region that is continuous, thus without gaps or breaks A one-dimensional temporal region can include as parts not only temporal intervals but also temporal instants separated from other parts by gaps.
examples: The year 2018.

classes.label: temporal instant
classes.definition: (Elucidation) A temporal instant is a zero-dimensional temporal region that has no proper temporal part
examples: The millennium

classes.label: Deflecting Prism
classes.definition: A Prism designed to deflect a beam of light entering the Prism by a fixed angle.

classes.label: Cooling Artifact Function
classes.definition: An Artifact Function that is realized in a process in which the thermal energy of a system decreases.

classes.label: Designative Name
classes.definition: A Designative Information Content Entity that consists of a string of characters that designates an entity within a specified cultural or social namespace and which is typically a word or phrase in a natural language that has an accepted cultural or social significance.

classes.label: Change
classes.definition: A Process in which some independent continuant endures and 1) one or more of the dependent entities it bears increase or decrease in intensity, 2) the entity begins to bear some dependent entity or 3) the entity ceases to bear some dependent entity.

classes.label: Act
classes.definition: A Process in which at least one Agent plays a causative role.

classes.label: Upper Midrange Frequency
classes.definition: A Sonic Frequency that is between 2 and 4 kHz.

classes.label: Natural Process
classes.definition: A Process existing in or produced by nature; rather than by the intent of human beings.

classes.label: Sound Frequency
classes.definition: A Frequency that is the rate of Oscillations per second of a Sound Wave.

classes.label: Mass Density
classes.definition: A Quality that inheres in a bearer in virtue of that bearer's mass per unit volume.

classes.label: Incorporated Organization
classes.definition: An Organization formed by an Act of Incorporation that consists of an association of individuals, created by law or under authority of law, having a continuous existence independent of the existences of its members and owners, and having powers and liabilities distinct from those of its members and owners.

classes.label: Nominal Stasis
classes.definition: A Stasis of Specifically Dependent Continuant in which some Independent Continuant bears a Quality or Realizable Entity that has a level of intensity or functionality that falls within the designed, expected, or acceptable range such that the Independent Continuant is of normal value, usefulness, or functionality.

classes.label: Propulsion Control System
classes.definition: A Control System that consists of control devices, displays, indicators, or modules designed to control a Propulsion System.

classes.label: Gain of Generically Dependent Continuant
classes.definition: A Gain of Dependent Continuant wherein some Independent Continuant becomes the carrier of some Generically Dependent Continuant.
examples: A Person forms a Plan, A Person is initiated into a Religion, A photgraphic image is produced.

classes.label: Shotgun
classes.definition: A Long Gun that fires packets of shot, a single slug, a sabot, or a specialty round (such as tear gas, bolo shell, or a breaching round) over shorter ranges than that of Rifles and with less accuracy.

classes.label: Triangular Waveform
classes.definition: A Waveform that is characterized by a triangular shape due to the continuous linear zig-zag transitions between minimum and maximum Amplitudes of the Wave Cycle.

classes.label: Minor Axis
classes.definition: A One-Dimensional Spatial Region that is the longest line segment perpendicular to the Major Axis that connects two points on the edge of an Ellipse.

classes.label: Title Document
classes.definition: A Legal Instrument that is designed as evidence of ownership.

classes.label: Power Inverting Artifact Function
classes.definition: A Current Conversion Artifact Function that is realized by processes in which some Material Artifact is used to convert direct current (DC) to alternating current (AC).

classes.label: Container
classes.definition: A Material Artifact that is designed to contain (wholly or partially) some material entity.

classes.label: Sensor Platform
classes.definition: A Material Entity that bears a Sensor Platform Artifact Function or Sensor Platform Role.

classes.label: Radio Communication Reception Artifact Function
classes.definition: A Communication Reception Artifact Function that is realized during events in which a Material Artifact receives information transmitted from another Material Artifact, where the transmission of information occurs using radio waves.

classes.label: Sensor Deployment Artifact Function
classes.definition: An Artifact Function that inheres in Material Artifacts that are designed to support or convey one or more Sensors while the Sensors are realizing their own Artifact Functions.

classes.label: Act of Advising
classes.definition: An Act of Directive Communication performed by providing advice or counsel to another agent.

classes.label: Electronic Stock
classes.definition: Stock that consists of Bytes.

classes.label: Hair Color
classes.definition: A Quality inhering in a portion of Hair by virtue of its color.

classes.label: Mailing
classes.definition: An Act of Communication by Media in which information concretized in tangible objects, usually written documents, are delivered to recipients.
parents: Act of Communication by Movement of Information Bearing Artifact

classes.label: Dispersive Prism
classes.definition: A Prism designed to break up a beam of light entering the Prism into its constituent spectral colors by leveraging the refractive index of light based on its Frequency.

classes.label: Median Point Estimate Information Content Entity
classes.definition: A Point Estimate Information Content Entity that is a measurement of a set of values and is equal to either the middle value or the average of the two values which separate the set into two equally populated upper and lower sets.

classes.label: Nuclear Reactor
classes.definition: A Power Source that is designed to initiate and control a self-sustained nuclear chain reaction to produce power in the form of heat, which can be transferred to a working fluid for further conversion to mechanical or electrical energy.

classes.label: Atmospheric Feature
classes.definition: A Geographic Feature that is part of the atmosphere (including the atmosphere itself as a non-proper part) having a relatively stable lifecycle and which has a location that can be distinguished from the surrounding portion of the atmosphere.

classes.label: Church
classes.definition: A Religious Facility that is designed for Christian worship and prayer.

classes.label: Decrease of Role
classes.definition: A Decrease of Realizable Entity in which some Independent Continuant has a decrease of some Role that it bears.

classes.label: Conveyance Artifact Function
classes.definition: A Motion Artifact Function that is realized in a process in which the bearer of the function conveys entities from one location to another.

classes.label: Soft X-ray Frequency
classes.definition: An X-Ray Frequency that is between 30 petahertz and 3 exahertz.

classes.label: Waste Management Artifact Function
classes.definition: A Service Artifact Function that is realized in processes of collecting, transporting, processing, recycling, monitoring, or disposing of waste materials.

classes.label: Act of Observation
classes.definition: A Planned Act of acquiring information from a source via the use of one or more senses.

classes.label: System Role
classes.definition: A Role that inheres in an entity in virtue of its parts or elements being arranged in such a way that they together exhibit behavior or meaning that they do not exhibit individually.

classes.label: Portion of Solid Fuel
classes.definition: A Portion of Fuel that is stored in a solid state.

classes.label: Grocery Store
classes.definition: A Commercial Facility that is designed to sell food.

classes.label: Hostel
classes.definition: A Residential Facility that is designed to temporarily lodge guests in a sociable environment for relatively low costs.

classes.label: Semicircular
classes.definition: A Shape quality inhering in a bearer in virtue of the bearer having the shape of half a circle.

classes.label: Portion of Solid Propellant
classes.definition: A Portion of Propellant that is stored in a solid state.

classes.label: Eye Color
classes.definition: A Quality inhering in an Eye by virtue of the color of the Eye's Iris.

classes.label: Petroleum Depot
classes.definition: A Storage Facility that is designed to store petroleum, oil, or lubricants.

classes.label: Province
classes.definition: A First-Order Administrative Region that is part of a Country and delimits the authority of a magistrate who holds constitutionally-defined administrative jurisdiction over the defined geographic territory that bounds the Province.

classes.label: Flow Control Valve
classes.definition: A Valve that is designed to regulate the flow or Pressure of a fluid. Flow Control Valves are often more complex than a simple Valve and typically include an Actuator that is capable of automatically adjusting the state of the valve in response to signals from a connected Sensor or Controller.

classes.label: Random Wire Antenna
classes.definition: A Wire Antenna that consists of a long wire suspended above the ground with a length that does not bear a relation to the wavelength of the radio waves used and which is typically used as a receiving antenna on the long, medium, and short wave bands.

classes.label: Banknote
classes.definition: A Portion of Cash that consists of a portable slips of paper or fabric designed to bear some specified Financial Value.

classes.label: Very High Frequency Communication Instrument
classes.definition: A Radio Communication Instrument that is designed to participate in some process that has process part some Very High Frequency.

classes.label: Act of Construction
classes.definition: An Act of Material Artifact Processing wherein Material Artifacts are built on site as prescribed by some contract. An Act of Construction typically involves the production of only one or a limited number of goods, such as in the construction of an airport or a community of condominiums.

classes.label: Religious Facility
classes.definition: A Facility that is designed for worship and prayer.

classes.label: Ground Motor Vehicle
classes.definition: A Ground Vehicle that is designed to receive its motive power from an Engine and is not designed to travel on rails.

classes.label: Stirling Engine
classes.definition: An External Combusion Engine that is designed to compress and expand some working fluid at different temperatures, such that there is a net conversion of heat energy to mechanical work.

classes.label: Healthcare Facility
classes.definition: A Facility that is designed for the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease.

classes.label: Reaction Engine
classes.definition: An Engine that provides propulsion by expelling Reaction Mass.

classes.label: Mobile Telephone
classes.definition: A Telephone that is connected to a Telephone Network by radio waves.

classes.label: Scalp Hair
classes.definition: A Bodily Component that consists of a portion of hair that grows on the scalp of a human or other animal.

classes.label: Telephone Line
classes.definition: A Telecommunication Network Line that consists of a physical wire or other signaling medium that is designed to be part of a Telephone Network.

classes.label: Open Pit Mine
classes.definition: A Mine that is designed to support the extraction of materials from the ground directly without using tunnels.

classes.label: Measurement Unit of Flow
classes.definition: A Measurement Unit that is used as a standard for measurement of the rate at which portions of a substance pass per unit of time.

classes.label: Frequency Measurement Artifact Function
classes.definition: A Measurement Artifact Function that is realized during events in which a Material Artifact is used to measure the Frequency of a specified object or class of objects.

classes.label: Multi-Hour Temporal Interval
classes.definition: A one-dimensional temporal region that is measured in Hours and spans at least one Hour. This is a defined class.

classes.label: Material Copy of a Book
classes.definition: A Material Copy of a Document that is designed to carry some specific Information Content Entity by means of ink, paper, parchment, or other materials fastened together to hinge at one side.

classes.label: Act of Location Change
classes.definition: An Act of Motion in which the location of some Object is changed by some Agent.

classes.label: Military Artifact Function
classes.definition: A Service Artifact Function that is realized in processes related to the armed services.

classes.label: Civil Time Reference System
classes.definition: A Temporal Reference System that is a statutory time scale as designated by civilian authorities to determine local time(s). In traditional astronomical usage, civil time is mean solar time as calculated from midnight as the beginning of the Civil Day.

classes.label: Three-Dimensional Path
classes.definition: A Three-Dimensional Spatial Region that encompasses the spatial region through which some Object travels.

classes.label: Material Copy of a Transcript
classes.definition: A Material Copy of a Document that is designed to carry some specific Information Content Entity that was originally recorded in a different medium.

classes.label: Ground Track Point
classes.definition: A Zero-Dimensional Spatial Region that is an idealized point located on the surface of an Astronomical Body directly below an Object Track Point.

classes.label: Town
classes.definition: A Local Administrative Region in which a human population permanently resides that is typically larger than the population of a Village but smaller than that of a City; is designated as a town based on a particular administrative, legal, or historical status; and which delimits a local Government that typically exercises less power than that of a City Government.

classes.label: Low Density Residential Area
classes.definition: A Populated Place where houses are on lots of more than one acre.

classes.label: Temporal Interval Identifier
classes.definition: A Temporal Region Identifier that designates some Temporal Interval.

classes.label: Measurement Unit of Acceleration
classes.definition: A Measurement Unit that is used as a standard for measurement of the rate at which objects change their velocities per unit of time.
examples: feet per second per second, kilometers per second per second

classes.label: Optical Microscope
classes.definition: A Microscope that is designed to use visible light and a system of Optical Lenses to produce a significantly enlarged image of the Object.

classes.label: Wired Communication Artifact Function
classes.definition: A Communication Artifact Function that is realized in a process that conveys meaningful signs by means of a (usually cylindrical) flexible strand or rod of metal.

classes.label: Code Identifier
classes.definition: A Non-Name Identifier that consists of a string of characters that was created and assigned according to an encoding system such that metadata can be derived from the identifier.

classes.label: Act of Estimation
classes.definition: An Act of Measuring that involves the comparison of a measurement of a similar Entity or of a portion of the Entity being estimated to produce an approximated measurement of the target Entity. Although the boundary between Act of Estimation and guessing is vague, estimation can be partially distinguished from guessing in that every Act of Estimation has as input some relevant information; whereas an act of guessing can occur sans information (or at least sans pertinent information). For example, if Mr. Green were asked how many blades of grass are in his lawn, he could simply choose a number (i.e. he could guess) or he could estimate the number by counting how many baldes of grass are in 1 square foot of his lawn, measuring the square footage of his lawn, and then multiplying these values to arrive at a number. Hence, many estimates may be loosely considered to be educated guesses.
examples: measuring how much time a train will add to your commute by measuring how long it takes for 10 train cars to pass a given point and then combining this information with an estimate of how many train cars are in a typical train based on your past experience
measuring the amount of time required to do a task based on how long it took to do a similar task in the past
measuring the height of a building by counting the number of floors and multiplying it by the height of an average floor in an average building
measuring the property value of a house based on its square footage and the average cost per square foot of other houses in the area

classes.label: Act of Social Movement
classes.definition: A Social Act composed of a series of performances, displays and campaigns directed at implementing, resisting or undoing a change in society.

classes.label: Standard Time of Day Identifier
classes.definition: A Time of Day Identifier that designates an approximate Temporal Instant that is part of some Day and is specified using the Hours, Minutes, and Seconds of the Day that preceded the Temporal Instant.

classes.label: Cutting Weapon
classes.definition: A Weapon that is designed to inflict harm, damage, or incapacity by means of separating some portion of its target into two or more portions through the application of acutely directed force.

classes.label: Green
classes.definition: A Color that is between Yellow and Cyan with a wavelength in the visible spectrum, typically between 520 to 560 nanometers.

classes.label: Process Ending
classes.definition: A Process Boundary that occupies a Zero-Dimensional Temporal Region that is the ending instant of the One-Dimensional Temporal Region that the Process, of which the Process Boundary is a part, occupies.

classes.label: Bodily Component
classes.definition: A Fiat Object Part located within or on the surface of an Agent.
examples: Bodily Components include anatomical structures, body flora, pathogens, toxins, and their combinations.

classes.label: Minute
classes.definition: A Temporal Interval that is equal to sixty consecutive Seconds.

classes.label: Autopilot System
classes.definition: A Vehicle Control System that is designed to enable some Agent to control the trajectory of a Vehicle without constant 'hands-on' control.

classes.label: Ordinal Date Identifier
classes.definition: A Decimal Date Identifier that designates some Day by using a number to indicate the sequential ordering of the Day since the beginning of the Year. An Ordinal Date Identifier may or may not also contain a number indicating a specific Year. If both numbers are included, the ISO 8601 ordinal date format stipulates that the two numbers be formatted as YYYY-DDD or YYYYDDD where [YYYY] indicates a year and [DDD] is the day of that year, from 001 through 365 (or 366 in leap years).

classes.label: Firearm
classes.definition: A Projectile Launcher that is designed to launch Bullets or Cartridges.

classes.label: Skill
classes.definition: An Agent Capability that inheres in a Person to the extent of that Person's capacity to realize it in Intentional Acts of a certain type.

classes.label: Infrared Telescope
classes.definition: A Telescope that is designed to aid in the observation of spatially distant Objects by means of collecting and focusing infrared light to form an enhanced image of the Object.

classes.label: Portion of Coolant
classes.definition: A Portion of Material that is designed to be used in a thermal control system to reduce or maintain the temperature of an object to or at a specified level.

classes.label: Bidirectional Transducer
classes.definition: A Transducer that is designed to receive a signal in the form of physical phenomena and convert it into an electrical signal, and vice versa.

classes.label: Preferred Stock
classes.definition: Stock that entitles its holder to receive a certain level of dividend payments before any dividends can be issued to other holders.

classes.label: Seat of National Government
classes.definition: A Government Building that is designed for the administration of a sovereign nation.
examples: Parliament of Canada
United States Capitol

classes.label: Control Surface
classes.definition: A Material Artifact that is designed to deflect air, water, or another medium around its surface in order to change the Attitude of a Vehicle by rotating the Vehicle on one or more of its Axes of Rotation.

classes.label: Propulsion System
classes.definition: A Material Artifact that is designed to facilitate the movement of material entities from one location to another and which consists of a source of mechanical power and a means of converting this power into propulsive force to generate the movement.

classes.label: Complex Optical Lens
classes.definition: An Optical Lens consisting of more than one Simple Optical Lenses.

classes.label: Electrical Artifact Function
classes.definition: An Artifact Function that is realized during events in which a Material Artifact is used to perform a process involving electrical power.

classes.label: Wave Process
classes.definition: A Natural Process that involves Oscillation accompanied by a transfer of energy that travels through a portion of matter or spatial region.

classes.label: Stasis of Partially Mission Capable
classes.definition: A Stasis of Mission Capability during which the participating Continuant is capable of performing some but not all of its primary functions for the specified Mission.

classes.label: Portion of Liquid Oxygen
classes.definition: A Portion of Cryogenic Material that is composed (almost) entirely of liquid oxygen.

classes.label: Skin Type
classes.definition: A Quality inhering in a portion of skin by virtue of its color and natural tendency to respond to ultraviolet light. Skin Type is classified according to a reference system such as the Fitzpatrick scale:

classes.label: Vehicle Compartment
classes.definition: A Material Artifact that is designed to partition a Vehicle into subdivisions for various purposes.

classes.label: Underwater Mine
classes.definition: A Mine that is designed to support the extraction of materials from the ocean floor.

classes.label: Square
classes.definition: A Rectangular shape which has four equal length sides and four 90 degree angles.

classes.label: End of Life Stasis
classes.definition: A Stasis of Artifact Operationality that holds during a Temporal Interval when the participating Material Artifact is no longer capable of realizing all of its designed primary Artifact Functions. An End of Life Stasis (EoL) is distinguished from a Stasis of Partially Mission Capable or Stasis of Non-Mission Capable in that EoL is more inclusive such that the participating Material Artifact may be either Partially or Non-Mission Capable. Additionally, EoL applies only to Artifacts and is typically determined in relation to its original mission and designed primary functions. In contrast, an Artifact's level of Mission Capability depends on the requirements of the mission under consideration such that a given Artifact may simultaneously be Fully Mission Capable for mission1, Partially Mission Capable for mission2, and Non-Mission Capable for mission3.

classes.label: Increase of Generically Dependent Continuant
classes.definition: An Increase of Dependent Continuant in which some Independent Continuant has an increase of some Generically Dependent Continuant that it bears.

classes.label: Rail Facility
classes.definition: A Transportation Facility that is designed for transferring people or cargo to and from Trains.

classes.label: Act of Military Force
classes.definition: A Planned Act of employing a Military Force to achieve some desired result.

classes.label: Mechanical Process
classes.definition: A Process that is the realization of some Disposition of a Material Artifact

classes.label: Air Inlet
classes.definition: A Fluid Control Artifact that consists of an opening that is designed to capture and direct the flow of air into the system it is part of.

classes.label: Translucent
classes.definition: An Opacity that inheres in a bearer in virtue of that bearer's capacity to transmit some but not all electromagnetic radiation of a given frequency through the bearer such that the bearer reflects, scatters, or absorbs some but not all electromagnetic radiation of that frequency.

classes.label: Ventilation Control Artifact Function
classes.definition: An Artifact Function that is realized in processes in which some Material Artifact is used to control the quality of air in some space.

classes.label: Unix Temporal Instant
classes.definition: A Temporal Instant as specified by the number of Seconds that have elapsed since the specified Epoch Time as described by an implementation of Unix Time.

classes.label: Stasis of Disposition
classes.definition: A Stasis of Realizable Entity in which some Independent Continuant bears some Disposition that remains unchanged during a Temporal Interval.

classes.label: Pump
classes.definition: A Fluid Control Artifact that is designed to impart motion to a portion of fluid to transport it within a system through the use of mechanical action.

classes.label: Information Processing Artifact
classes.definition: A Material Artifact that is designed to use algorithms to transform some Information Content Entity into another Information Content Entity.

classes.label: Artifact Function Specification
classes.definition: A Prescriptive Information Content Entity that prescribes some Material Artifact Function and which is part of some Material Artifact Model.

classes.label: Spatial Orientation
classes.definition: A Relational Quality that is the angle of Rotation of an Object relative to one or more Plane of Reference or Axis of Rotation.

classes.label: Measurement Unit
classes.definition: A Descriptive Information Content Entity that describes a definite magnitude of a physical quantity, defined and adopted by convention and/or by law, that is used as a standard for measurement of the same physical quantity.

classes.label: Act of Conducting Mass Media Interview
classes.definition: An Act of Mass Media Communication involving a conversation between a reporter and a person of public interest, used as a basis of a broadcast or publication.

classes.label: Vehicle Track Point
classes.definition: An Object Track Point that is where a Vehicle is or was located during some motion.

classes.label: Act of Expressive Communication
classes.definition: An Act of Communication in which an Agent expresses their attitudes or emotions towards some entity. Examples: apologizing, condoling, congratulating, greeting, thanking, accepting (acknowledging an acknowledgment)

classes.label: Solar Time Reference System
classes.definition: A Temporal Reference System that is based on the position of the Sun in the sky.

classes.label: Bounding Box Point
classes.definition: A Geospatial Position that is a proper part of some Geospatial Region Bounding Box.

classes.label: First-Order Administrative Region
classes.definition: A Government Domain that is a primary administrative division of a Country.
examples: a state in the United States

classes.label: Performance Specification
classes.definition: A Prescriptive Information Content Entity that prescribes some aspect of the behavior of a participant in a Process given one or more operating conditions.
examples: Maximum Speed at high altitude; Rate of Ascent at 10 degrees celsius with nominal payload.

classes.label: Portion of Liquid Hydrogen
classes.definition: A Portion of Cryogenic Material that is composed (almost) entirely of liquid hydrogen.

classes.label: Tattoo
classes.definition: A Bodily Component that consists of a typically permanent mark or design on a portion of skin that is created by a process of pricking and ingraining an indelible pigment or by raising scars.

classes.label: Power Transformer
classes.definition: A Material Artifact that is designed to transfer electrical energy between two or more circuits through electromagnetic induction.

classes.label: Increase of Quality
classes.definition: An Increase of Specifically Dependent Continuant in which some Indpendent Continuant has an increase of some Quality that it bears.

classes.label: Recording Device
classes.definition: An Information Processing Artifact that is designed to capture some information and store it in some recording format on some storage medium.

classes.label: Act of Directive Communication
classes.definition: An Act of Communication that is intended to cause the hearer to take a particular action. Examples: advising, admonishing, asking, begging, dismissing, excusing, forbidding, instructing, ordering, permitting, requesting, requiring, suggesting, urging, warning

classes.label: Third-Order Administrative Region
classes.definition: A Government Domain that is a subdivision of a Second-Order Administrative Region.

classes.label: Stasis of Specifically Dependent Continuant
classes.definition: A Stasis in which some Independent Continuant bears some Specifically Dependent Continuant that remains unchanged during a Temporal Interval.

classes.label: Optical Instrument
classes.definition: A Material Artifact that is designed to process light waves. Light waves can be processed in a variety of ways including via reflection, refraction, diffraction, deflection, focusing, collimation, dispersion, and interference.

classes.label: Act of Financial Deposit
classes.definition: An Act of Financial Instrument Use wherein a Financial Instrument is transferred by an Agent (the Depositor) to another Agent to create a liability to be repaid to the Depositor through an Act of Financial Withdrawal.

classes.label: Maximum Power
classes.definition: A Power that is characterized by the maximum rate of Work, or Energy consumed, done in a given time period.

classes.label: Domain of a Country
classes.definition: A Government Domain that is associated with certain distinct political, ethnic, or cultural characteristics, and which delimits a Government that has legitimate authority over a Populace.

classes.label: Measurement Unit of Amount of Substance
classes.definition: A Measurement Unit that is used as a standard for measurement of the number of a specified type of particle in a portion of matter. The type of particle quantified is typically either atoms or molecules, but may also be protons, neutrons, electrons, quarks, or other particles. The type of particle being measured should always be specified along with the measurement and its unit.
examples: mole, pound-mole

classes.label: Populace
classes.definition: A Group of Persons forming the total population of some Government Domain.

classes.label: Act of Government
classes.definition: A Planned Act that is initiated or supported by some Geopolitical Entity and enforced by some Government Agent.

classes.label: Cargo Cabin
classes.definition: A Vehicle Compartment that is used to store goods or materials during transportation.

classes.label: Act of Meeting
classes.definition: An Act of Association wherein two or more Persons assemble for some common purpose.

classes.label: Incendiary Weapon
classes.definition: A Weapon that is designed to inflict harm, damage, or incapacity by means of starting a fire.

classes.label: Artificial Language
classes.definition: A Language that is developed through conscious planning and premeditation, rather than one that was developed through use and repetition.
examples: Esperanto
Python Programming Language

classes.label: Flight Transponder
classes.definition: A Radio Transponder that is designed to produce a specified response (typically for identification, location, or status update purposes) when it receives a radio-frequency interrogation.

classes.label: Clockwise Rotational Motion
classes.definition: A Rotational Motion in which the direction of rotation is toward the right as seen relative to the designated side of the plane of rotation.
examples: the axial rotation of the Earth as seen from above the South Pole

classes.label: Instant Messaging
classes.definition: An Act of Communication Mediated by Artifact in which real-time direct text-based communication occurs between two or more Agents using personal computers or other devices, along with shared Instant Messaging Client Software conveyed over a computer network.
parents: Act of Communication Mediated by Artifact

classes.label: Radio Frequency
classes.definition: An Electromagnetic Radiation Frequency of some Electromagnetic Wave that is between 3 kHz and 300 GHz.

classes.label: Act of Reporting
classes.definition: An Act of Representative Communication performed by giving a detailed account or statement.

classes.label: Telephone Network
classes.definition: A Telecommunication Network that is designed to allow telephone calls to be made between two or more parties connected to the network.

classes.label: Generator Control Unit
classes.definition: A Control System that is designed to regulate the voltage of some Electrical Power Source.

classes.label: Mode Point Estimate Information Content Entity
classes.definition: A Point Estimate Information Content Entity that is a measurement of a set of values and is equal to the value or values that occur most often in the set. While there is always at least one Mode for every set of data, it is possible for any given set of data to have multiple Modes. The Mode is typically most useful when the members of the set are all Nominal Measurement Information Content Entities.

classes.label: Near Infrared Light Frequency
classes.definition: An Infrared Light Frequency that is between 214 and 400 terahertz.

classes.label: Hand Gun
classes.definition: A Firearm that is designed to have a relatively short barrel and to be held in one or two hands and to be fired without being braced against the shoulder.

classes.label: Facial Hair
classes.definition: A Bodily Component that consists of a portion of hair that grows on the face of a human (typically male) or other animal.

classes.label: Lithium-ion Electric Battery
classes.definition: A Secondary Cell Electric Battery that produces electricity when lithium ions move from anode to cathode.

classes.label: Material Copy of a Timekeeping Instrument
classes.definition: An Information Bearing Artifact that is designed to carry some specific Information Content Entity that is about some temporal region.

classes.label: Manual Tool
classes.definition: A Tool that is designed to be powered by manual labor rather than by an engine.

classes.label: Coordinate System Axis
classes.definition: A One-Dimensional Spatial Region defined by a Coordinate System for the purpose of identifying the position of entities along one dimension of the Coordinate System's spatial framework.

classes.label: Electrical Connector Artifact Function
classes.definition: An Electrical Conduction Artifact Function that is realized by processes in which some Material Artifact is used to join electrical terminations to create an electrical circuit.

classes.label: z-Axis
classes.definition: A Coordinate System Axis designated by the variable 'z'.

classes.label: Minimum Ordinal Measurement Information Content Entity
classes.definition: An Ordinal Measurement Information Content Entity that is a measurement of some entity in virtue of it being the smallest or having the least amount relative to a nominally described set of like entities.

classes.label: Criminal Act
classes.definition: A Planned Act committed in violation of rules or laws for which some governing authority (via mechanisms such as legal systems) can prescribe a conviction.

classes.label: Wave Cycle
classes.definition: A Wave Process that consists of a portion of a Wave Process that begins at an arbitrary point of the Wave Process and ends at the next point when the pattern of the Wave Process begins to repeat.

classes.label: Large-Scale Rocket Launcher
classes.definition: A Rocket Launcher that is designed to contain multiple Rocket Launchers.

classes.label: Act of Interpersonal Relationship
classes.definition: An Act of Association between two or more Persons that may range from fleeting to enduring.

classes.label: Very High Frequency
classes.definition: A Radio Frequency that is between 30 and 300 MHz. The corresponding Wavelength range is 10–1 m

classes.label: Object Track Point
classes.definition: A Zero-Dimensional Spatial Region that is an idealized point where an Object is or was located during some motion.

classes.label: Detergent Artifact Function
classes.definition: A Surfactant Artifact Function that is realized in a process that cleans substances in dilute solutions.

classes.label: Base of Operations
classes.definition: A Military Base with permanently stationed operating forces, robust Infrastructure, and strengthened force protection measures such that it is designed to launch and support large-scale operations, support smaller or less-permanent bases, and organize supply facilities.

classes.label: Civilian Role
classes.definition: A Role that inheres in an Agent or Group of Agents by virtue of that Agent or Group of Agents not being part of either an Armed Force or police force.

classes.label: Ultraviolet Telescope
classes.definition: A Telescope that is designed to aid in the observation of spatially distant Objects by means of collecting and focusing ultraviolet light to form an enhanced image of the Object.

classes.label: Organization Member Role
classes.definition: A Role that inheres in an Agent in virtue of the responsibilities that Agent is expected to fulfill as a member of some Organization.

classes.label: Geopolitical Organization
classes.definition: An Organization that bears a Geopolitical Power Role.

classes.label: Affordance
classes.definition: A Realizable Entity of an Independent Continuant that creates an opportunity for an Agent to realize some Agent Capability or Disposition in some Act.

classes.label: Arrow
classes.definition: A Portion of Ammunition that is designed to be fired from a Bow and consists of a long straight stiff shaft with stabilizers (fletchings) and a slot (the nock) on one end and a weighted tip (the arrowhead) on the other end.

classes.label: Thrust
classes.definition: A Force that is equal in magnitude to but in the opposite direction of an exerted Force and which is used to describe the forward Force of a Jet or Rocket Engine in reaction to the Acceleration of its Reaction Mass in the opposite direction. More generally, Thrust is the propulsive Force of a Rocket.

classes.label: Hotel
classes.definition: A Residential Facility that is designed to provide lodging that is paid for on a short-term basis.

classes.label: Language Skill
classes.definition: A Skill that is realized by an Act which is prescribed by a Language.

classes.label: Act of Thanking
classes.definition: An Act of Expressive Communication performed by expressing gratitude.

classes.label: Fragrance Artifact Function
classes.definition: An Artifact Function that is realized in processes of emitting a pleasant or sweet odor.

classes.label: Axial Rotation Period
classes.definition: A Temporal Interval that is equal to the length of time required for a spinning Object to complete one rotation around its Axis of Rotation.

classes.label: Blunt
classes.definition: A Shape Quality inhering in a bearer in virtue of the bearer not having a sharp edge or point.

classes.label: Artifact Version Ordinality
classes.definition: An Ordinal Measurement Information Content Entity that is about the form of a Material Artifact which differs in some respects from previous or future forms of that Material Artifact.

classes.label: Authority Role
classes.definition: A Role that is realized by Processes which create, modify, transfer, or eliminate Process Regulations or other Authority Roles, and inheres in an Agent in virtue of collective acceptance of that Agent's ability to issue binding directives. Authority Roles are externally grounded in a social group's collective acceptance of the binding force of the agent's directives. This acceptance can be direct or indirect (e.g., by accepting a procedure for deputizing authority). Such collective acceptance need not be explicit or cognized; rather, collective acceptance can be expressed in the dispositions and attitudes of people toward that agent's directives. In many cases, the directives issued by Authority Roles are backed by threats of punishment or sanction for failure to comply, but the issuing of a directive plus a threat is not sufficient for authority. Rather, an agent's authority must be accepted either directly or indirectly through the acceptance of a procedure for bestowing authority (e.g., elections).

classes.label: Ground Track
classes.definition: A One-Dimensional Spatial Region defined by the line formed on the surface of an Astronomical Body by projecting an imaginary line from the center of the tracked Object to the center of the Astronomical Body as the Object travels above the surface. The Ground Track is the line on the surface of the Earth or other Astronomical Body that is located directly below the Object Track.

classes.label: Material Copy of a Certificate
classes.definition: An Information Bearing Artifact that bears an Information Content Entity which attests to certain demonstrated characteristics of an Object, Person, or Organization.

classes.label: Minimum Speed Artifact Function
classes.definition: A Speed Artifact Function that is realized in some process in which the Material Artifact bearing the Artifact Function attains the lowest speed at which that Material Artifact is designed to operate.

classes.label: Act of Homicide
classes.definition: An Act of Violence which causes the unlawful killing of another person.

classes.label: Facility
classes.definition: A Material Artifact that is designed as a building or campus dedicated to some specific purpose.

classes.label: Telephone Subscriber Line
classes.definition: A Telephone Line that connects a Communication Endpoint to another node in a Telecommunication Network to enable service to a user's Telephone.

classes.label: Electrical Contact Artifact Function
classes.definition: An Electrical Conduction Artifact Function that is realized by processes in which some Material Artifact is used as an endpoint of an electrical circuit from which an electrical current is passed via physical contact with the endpoint.

classes.label: Heliport
classes.definition: An Airport that is designed for launching, receiving, and housing Rotorcraft.

classes.label: Purple
classes.definition: A Color that is aproximately midway between Red and Blue.

classes.label: Process Beginning
classes.definition: A Process Boundary that occupies a Zero-Dimensional Temporal Region that is the starting instant of the One-Dimensional Temporal Region that the Process, of which the Process Boundary is a part, occupies.

classes.label: Measurement Unit of Sound Level
classes.definition: A Measurement Unit that is used as a standard for measurement of the level (the loudness) of sounds.
examples: decibels, sones

classes.label: Camera
classes.definition: An Imaging Instrument that is designed to form and digitally or physically record an image of an entity.

classes.label: Act of Pilgrimage
classes.definition: An Act of Travel to a location of importance to a person's beliefs and faith.

classes.label: Act of Change of Residence
classes.definition: An Act of Location Change involving one or more Persons moving from one place of residence to another.

classes.label: Act of Terrorist Training Instruction
classes.definition: An Act of Training Instruction performed by an Agent who realizes a capacity derived from the Agent's affiliation with some Terrorist Organization by imparting knowledge of the tactics, techniques, and/or strategies of the use of violence against civilians in order to attain goals that are political, religous, or ideological in nature to an Agent either directly or indirectly through some communication medium.

classes.label: Event Status Nominal Information Content Entity
classes.definition: A Nominal Measurement Information Content Entity that is a measurement of the current state of a process.
examples: proposed, approved, planned, in progress, completed, failed, or successful

classes.label: Rifle
classes.definition: A Long Gun that is designed to have a rifled barrel and to fire single Bullets over long ranges with high accuracy.

classes.label: Object Track
classes.definition: A One-Dimensional Spatial Region that consists of the idealized line along which an Object has traversed during some motion. The exact line of the Object Track may be drawn based on the Center of Mass of the Object or another reference point, such as the location of a transponder beacon or the center of a radar cross-section, depending on the Object being tracked.

classes.label: Friction Reduction Artifact Function
classes.definition: An Artifact Function that is realized in processes of reducing the force resisting the relative motion of surfaces in contact.

classes.label: One-Dimensional Geospatial Boundary
classes.definition: A Fiat Line that is a boundary of some Geospatial Region.

classes.label: Act of Congratulating
classes.definition: An Act of Expressive Communication performed by expressing vicarious pleasure to a person on the occasion of their success or good fortune.

classes.label: Sound Wavelength
classes.definition: A Wavelength that is the distance a Sound Wave traverses during one Wave Cycle.

classes.label: Engine
classes.definition: A Material Artifact that is designed to convert one form of energy into mechanical energy.

classes.label: Multi-Day Temporal Interval
classes.definition: A one-dimensional temporal region that is measured in Days and spans at least one Day. This is a defined class.

classes.label: Chemical Weapon
classes.definition: A Weapon that is designed to inflict harm, damage, or incapacity by means of releasing toxic chemicals.

classes.label: Subcontinent
classes.definition: A Geospatial Region that is bounded by a large, relatively self-contained landmass forming a subdivision of a Continent.

classes.label: Moving Target Indication Artifact Function
classes.definition: A Radar Imaging Artifact Function that inheres in Material Artifacts that are designed to identify and produce visual representations of moving entities by using a radar to emit successive phase coherent pulses, which are sampled and added to the subsequent pulse to cancel out signals from non-moving entities such that only signals from moving entities remain and are displayed.

classes.label: Radio Telescope
classes.definition: A Telescope that is designed to aid in the observation of spatially distant Objects by means of collecting and focusing radio waves to form an enhanced image of the Object. A Radio Telescope consists of a specialized Antenna and a Radio Receiver and is typically used to receive radio waves from sources in outer space.

classes.label: Shell
classes.definition: A Portion of Ammunition that is designed to be a non-self-propelled projectile and to carry a payload (explosive or other) over a relatively short distance.

classes.label: Measurement Unit of Area
classes.definition: A Measurement Unit that is used as a standard for measurement of two-dimensional regions or Geospatial Regions.
examples: square feet, square meters, acre, hectare

classes.label: Major Axis
classes.definition: A One-Dimensional Spatial Region that is the longest line segment that connects two points on the edge of an Ellipse.

classes.label: Reflecting Optical Telescope
classes.definition: An Optical Telescope that is designed to aid in the observation of spatially distant Objects by means of collecting and focusing visible light via reflection through the use of one or more curved Mirrors to form an enhanced image of the Object.

classes.label: Ammunition Depot
classes.definition: A Storage Facility that is designed to store Portions of Ammunition.

classes.label: Semi-Minor Axis
classes.definition: A One-Dimensional Spatial Region that is equal to half the length of the Minor Axis of an Ellipse.

classes.label: Presence Frequency
classes.definition: A Sonic Frequency that is between 4 and 6 kHz.

classes.label: Time of Day
classes.definition: A Temporal Instant that is part of a Day.

classes.label: Populated place
classes.definition: An Anthropogenic Feature at which people live or have lived.

classes.label: Month
classes.definition: A Temporal Interval that is based on the approximate length of time required for a Natural Satellite to complete one cycle of its rotational motion around its Primary Body. Unless otherwise specified, it is assumed that a Month is specified relative to the Rotational Motion of the Moon around the Earth. Earth Months are approximately equal to four consecutive Weeks or 30 consecutive Days.

classes.label: Transportation Facility
classes.definition: A Facility that is designed for commencing or concluding the transportation of transportation artifacts, or for housing transportation artifacts.

classes.label: Julian Year
classes.definition: A Calendar Year in the Julian Calendar. A Julian Year begins concurrently with January 1, ends concurrently with December 31, and has an average duration of exactly 365.25 Julian Days. Julian Years are typically indicated by prefixing a capital 'J' in front of the Year number, e.g. J2000.0 or J2018.

classes.label: Planned Act
classes.definition: An Act in which at least one Agent plays a causative role and which is prescribed by some Directive Information Content Entity held by at least one of the Agents.

classes.label: Measurement Unit of Power
classes.definition: A Measurement Unit that is used as a standard for measurement of rates of work.
examples: watt, horsepower

classes.label: Diffraction Grating
classes.definition: An Optical Instrument with a periodic structure that is designed to split and defract a beam of light into several beams travelling in different directions.

classes.label: Torpedo Tube
classes.definition: A Projectile Launcher that is designed to launch Torpedoes.

classes.label: Pumping Station
classes.definition: A Product Transport Facility that is designed to pump fluids from one place to another.

classes.label: Stock Certificate
classes.definition: Stock that consists of a Certificate.

classes.label: Act of Training
classes.definition: A Planned Act in which knowledge, skills or values are imparted from one or more Agents to at least one other Agent.

classes.label: Act of Vocational Training Acquisition
classes.definition: An Act of Training Acquisition performed by an Agent by acquiring skills required for a specific occupation in industry, agriculture or trade from an Agent or communication medium that realizes a capacity derived from its affiliation with a Vocational School, Technical School, Trade Organization, or Industry Educational Program Provider.

classes.label: Lighting System
classes.definition: A Material Artifact that is designed to emit light within some area.

classes.label: Act of Terrorist Training Acquisition
classes.definition: An Act of Training Acquisition performed by an Agent by acquiring knowledge of the tactics, techniques, and/or strategies of the use of violence against civilians in order to attain goals that are political, religous, or ideological in nature from an Agent or communication medium that realizes a capacity derived from its affiliation with a Terrorist Organization.

classes.label: Propeller
classes.definition: A Material Artifact that is designed to convert rotary motion from an Engine or other mechanical Power Source into propulsive Force.

classes.label: Measurement Unit of Mass
classes.definition: A Measurement Unit that is used as a standard for measurement of an object's resistance to Acceleration when a Force is applied to the object.
examples: ounce, gram, pound

classes.label: Act of Oath Taking
classes.definition: An Act of Commissive Communication performed by stating or promising, usually calling upon something or someone that the oath maker considers sacred.

classes.label: Heat Sink
classes.definition: A Material Artifact that is designed to regulate the temperature of a computer by the passive transfer of heat away from other components in the computer.

classes.label: Fragmentation Artifact Function
classes.definition: A Damaging Artifact Function that is realized in a process in which the structural integrity of an entity is impaired because of a detonation which causes fragmentation.

classes.label: Petroleum Manufacturing Facility
classes.definition: A Factory that is designed to manufacture petroleum-based products.

classes.label: Stasis of Realizable Entity
classes.definition: A Stasis of Specifically Dependent Continuant in which some Independent Continuant bears some Realizable Entity that remains unchanged during a Temporal Interval.

classes.label: Road
classes.definition: A Land Transportation Artifact that is designed to enable Ground Vehicles to travel from one location to another.

classes.label: Chemical Manufacturing Facility
classes.definition: A Factory that is designed to manufacture or process chemicals.

classes.label: Shaft
classes.definition: A Material Artifact that is designed to rotate and transmit Torque, Power, or Rotational Motion from one machine element to another. A Shaft is usually used to connect other components of a drive train that cannot be connected directly either because of the distance between them or the need to allow for relative movement between those components.

classes.label: Loss of Realizable Entity
classes.definition: A Loss of Specifically Dependent Continuant in which some Independent Continuant ceases to be the bearer of some Realizable Entity.

classes.label: Continent
classes.definition: A Geospatial Region that is bounded by any of the Earth's main continuous expanses of land.

classes.label: Nozzle
classes.definition: A Fluid Control Artifact that is designed to control the speed, direction, rate, shape, or pressure of the flow of fluid exiting it.

classes.label: Information Bearing Entity
classes.definition: An Object upon which an Information Content Entity generically depends. This class continues to use the word ‘bearing’ in its rdfslabel because of potential confusion with the acronym ‘ICE’, which is widely used for information content entity.

classes.label: Transportation Artifact
classes.definition: A Material Artifact that is fixed in place and designed to enable the movement of Vehicles and Agents from one location to another.

classes.label: Portion of Cryogenic Material
classes.definition: A Portion of Material that has been reduced to a very low temperature (below -180 degrees Celcius).

classes.label: Fluid Control Artifact
classes.definition: A Material Artifact that is designed to manipulate the flow of a fluid (i.e. a liquid or a gas).

classes.label: Radiopaque
classes.definition: A Radiopacity that inheres in a bearer in virtue of its capacity to prevent most X-rays from passing through it.

classes.label: Calendar Month
classes.definition: A Month that begins and ends concurrently with the Days specified by a Calendar System to be the first and last Days of the Month.
examples: January; February; March; April; May; June; July; August; September; October; November; December

classes.label: Muzzle Blast
classes.definition: A Sound Wave Process that is caused by a projectile being pushed from the barrel of a firearm by an explosive charge.

classes.label: Gamma Ray Frequency
classes.definition: An Electromagnetic Radiation Frequency of some Electromagnetic Wave that is above 30 exahertz. Currently gamma radiation is distinguished from x-rays by their source--either inside or outside of the nucleus--rather than by frequency, energy, and wavelength.

classes.label: Shop
classes.definition: A Commercial Facility designed to sell small lots of goods to consumers.

classes.label: Clock Time System
classes.definition: A Temporal Reference System that is a convention for keeping and displaying the Time of Day. A single Clock Time System does not provide a complete means for identifying or measuring times. Depending on the particular Clock Time System, it may be compatible for use with one or more other Temporal Reference Systems.

classes.label: Hydraulic Fluid Reservoir
classes.definition: A Container that is designed to store some hydraulic fluid for use in some Hyrdraulic Power Source.

classes.label: Election
classes.definition: A Social Act by which a population chooses an individual to hold public office.

classes.label: Hearing Aid
classes.definition: A Medical Artifact that is designed to improve hearing for its user.

classes.label: Catalyst Artifact Function
classes.definition: A Chemical Reaction Artifact Function that is realized in a process in which the rate of a chemical reaction is increased due to the participation of an additional substance, without that substance being consumed in the reaction.

classes.label: Cannon
classes.definition: A Projectile Launcher that is designed to use a controlled explosion to launch a relatively large Portion of Ammunition, such as a Round Shot or a Shell, at a significant Velocity.

classes.label: Radio Transmitter
classes.definition: A Radio Communication Instrument that is an electronic device that is designed to generate a radio frequency alternating current, which can be applied to a Radio Antenna to be transmitted as radio waves.

classes.label: Educational Facility
classes.definition: A Facility that is designed for facilitating learning, or the acquisition of knowledge, skills, values, beliefs, and habits.

classes.label: Underground Mine
classes.definition: A Mine that is designed to support the extraction of materials from the ground using underground tunnels and shafts.

classes.label: Combustion
classes.definition: A Natural Process in which a Portion of Fuel or other Material Entity is burned.

classes.label: Communication Interference Artifact Function
classes.definition: An Artifact Function that is realized during events in which a Material Artifact is used to interfere with the transmission of information for the purpose of preventing communication.

classes.label: Armed Force
classes.definition: An Organization having the Objective to further the foreign and domestic policies of a Government and to defend that body and the nation it represents from external and internal aggressors.

classes.label: Spatial Reference System
classes.definition: A Reference System that describes a set of standards for uniquely identifying the position of an entity or the direction of a vector within a defined spatial region by means of measurements along one or more Coordinate System Axes. Note that, while reference systems and reference frames are treated as synonyms here, some people treat them as related but separate entities. See:

classes.label: Solar Calendar System
classes.definition: A Calendar System that is designed to organize and identify dates based on the cycles of an Astronomical Body's Orbit around the Sun. Unless otherwise specified, a Solar Calendar System is assumed to be relative to the Orbit of the Earth around the Sun.

classes.label: Nuclear Weapon
classes.definition: A Weapon that is designed to inflict harm, damage, or incapacity by means of a destructive nuclear reaction, either through fission or through a combination of fission and fusion.

classes.label: Momentum
classes.definition: A Process Profile of an object in Motion that is the product of its Mass and Velocity with respect to a frame of reference. The SI unit of measure for Momentum is Newton seconds (N s).

classes.label: Enemy Role
classes.definition: An Allegiance Role that inheres in an Agent by virtue of that Agent having committed offensive Acts or exhibited intent to perform such Acts towards a particular Agent or Group of Agents or has been declared as hostile by some appropriate authority.

classes.label: Torpedo
classes.definition: A Precision-Guided Missile that is designed to be fired into a body of water, be self-propelled through the water, and carry an explosive payload.

classes.label: Albedo
classes.definition: A Radiation Reflectivity that inheres in a bearer in virtue of the capacity of its surface to reflect incident electromagnetic radiation of a particular wavelength. Albedo is a reflection coefficient and is measured as the ratio of radiation reflected from the surface to the incident radiation. Albedo is dimensionless, can be expressed as a percentage, and is measured on a scale from 0 for no reflection to 1 for perfect reflection of a surface. Albedo depends on the wavelength of the radiation; when no wavelength is specified, it typically refers to some appropriate average across the spectrum of visible light.

classes.label: Counterfeit Financial Instrument
classes.definition: A Counterfeit Instrument that is designed to be a fake replica of some legally sanctioned Financial Instrument.

classes.label: Cylindrical
classes.definition: A Three Dimensional Shape inhering in a bearer in virtue of the bearer having an elongated shape with round bases.

classes.label: Strength
classes.definition: A Realizable Entity that is realized when its bearer exerts or resists some power, influence, or force. Strength is intended to be understood broadly here. Physical strength is only one type of Strength. Other subtypes of Strength may include military strength, psychological strength, emotional strength, political strength, technological strength, and so on.

classes.label: Emergency Locator Transmitter
classes.definition: A Radio Transmitter that is designed to signal distress and provide positional data for the entity it is located on.

classes.label: Stasis of Partially Mission Capable Maintenance
classes.definition: A Stasis of Partially Mission Capable during which the participating Continuant is not capable of performing some of its primary functions for the specified Mission due to participating in an Act Of Maintenance.

classes.label: Inertial Navigation System
classes.definition: A Navigation System that is designed to continuously calculate via dead reckoning the position, orientation, and velocity of a moving object without the need for external references.

classes.label: Power Source
classes.definition: A Material Artifact that is designed to supply power to some other Material Artifact.

classes.label: Radar Imaging Artifact Function
classes.definition: An Imaging Artifact Function that inheres in Material Artifacts that are designed to produce visual representations of entities using radio waves.

classes.label: Decrease of Specifically Dependent Continuant
classes.definition: A Decrease of Dependent Continuant in which some Independent Continuant has a decrease in some Specifically Dependent Continuant that it bears.

classes.label: Act of Decoy Use
